video_title: Willie Cauley-Stein tells all on taking 10-15 Percs a day and gambling with his LIFE everyday 😳

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on his heavy Percocet usage while playing
quotes.excerpt: I was doing 10-15 of them bitches a day and they ended up being laced with fentanyl.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: We see the Brandon Clarke situation, bro, and that shit is sad. If it really was what they said it was, bro, like...

text_blocks.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
text_blocks.text: No, it's going on. That's what I'm asking. For real, because that could have been me. I was doing 10-15 of them bitches a day and they ended up being laced with fentanyl. At any of those, not one of those was safe. So as we hear about this shit on these rap songs, take a Percocet and you know how they want to make Percocet rhyme with a motherfucker. I want you to break it down to our viewers. Man, your ass can be in six feet under.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the dangers of pill dependency in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: You gambling with your life every time you bust one down.
quotes.quote: You don't know. It's all a gamble, bro. You gambling with your life every time you bust one down. And you think that your partner has a plug that's getting them real, but he don't. Them bitches ain't real. They just trying to get the money. It's one of them things, bro, where it was tough. It was a tough because we went from having real ones to fake ones. Years before that, we was on the real ones, getting scripts from old ladies. We picking them up. So you know it, but then you on them, so now you need it. Now I needed it to go to work, bro. That's where it was getting. It was about escaping reality, dog.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the personal tragedies that fueled his addiction
quotes.excerpt: I went through like five deaths in my circle in like a two-three year span.
quotes.quote: It was about escaping reality, dog. My partner just got murdered by my other partner. Then my little brother passed away from an overdose. This is all in the same year. And then my grandpa dies the next few months after that. I went through like five deaths in my circle in like a two-three year span and I didn't process not one of them deaths because I'm hooping. I'm not going to see my grandfather in hospice because I got a game in Utah. I'm missing out on these things because I'm playing the game of basketball. And then now the game of basketball ain't serving me no more. So now I'm really in an emotional standpoint of like, I'm trying to just go to sleep.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on keeping his addiction hidden from teammates
quotes.excerpt: Nobody knew that I was on them shits till I told everybody I was on them shits.
quotes.quote: Nobody knew that I was on them shits till I told everybody I was on them shits. They just thought I didn't love basketball no more. But I just didn't have nothing. I'm literally ripping a 30 before I come into the game. Going into the locker room ripping a 30. It just start with one thing and it ends up now you're dependent on it. Now I felt like, oh, I'm going to go through dope sickness. You got to be a voice for this shit, bro.

quotes.speaker: Willie Cauley-Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Willie Cauley-Stein on the glorification of drug use in hip-hop and sports
quotes.excerpt: I was in the peak of it, bro, 2015, the heart of fucking rap music and basketball.
quotes.quote: I was in the peak of it, bro, 2015, the heart of fucking rap music and basketball, and it's glorified. And so there's a point where, you know, it could be influential. It is influential, bro. Future one of my favorite rappers of all time, and I'm going in, and this is serious. And I'm going in and I'm like seeing these rappers that glorify drugs, but I'm a professional artist or a professional hooper that politically you can't do drugs. But that guy gets paid millions of dollars. He's going to get put on in our arenas. They're going to bring him to the games. But I do that shit and it's a problem. But we glorify it on the other side of even as a basketball program, we still glorify that rapper that's coming in your gym singing about doing Percocets.
